dishes.make_ahead: Cut up to 4 hours ahead, keep in cold water then dry well

steps.text: Cut the potatoes into chips, rinse in cold water and dry thoroughly with a clean tea towel.
Heat the oil in a sturdy deep pan to 140C and blanch the chips in batches for 5 minutes without browning.
Drain and cool the chips for 15 minutes (this rest is part of the cook time).
Raise the oil to 185C and fry in batches until crisp, drain, season with salt and serve in paper boats.

dishes.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Divide the mince into four loose balls and slice the onion very thin.
Heat a griddle until very hot. Put the beef balls on it, top with onion and press firmly into thin patties. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook 3 minutes, flip and cook a further 2 to 3 minutes until the centre reaches 75C. Lay the cheese on top to melt.
Toast the buns and fill with the patties, pickles and mustard.

veg.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Divide the plant-based mince into four loose balls and slice the onion very thin.
Heat a griddle until very hot. Put the mince balls on it, top with onion and press firmly into thin patties. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes until well browned, flip and cook a further 2 minutes. Lay the cheese on top to melt.
Toast the buns and fill with the patties, pickles and mustard.
Lay the bacon in a cold frying pan and cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until crisp. Lift out onto a plate.
Fry the eggs in the bacon fat, spooning the fat over the yolks until the whites are set.
Meanwhile toast the white bread and spread with the butter.
Plate the eggs with the bacon and buttered toast.
Fry the mushrooms in the olive oil over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and crisp at the edges. Stir through the smoked paprika and soy sauce and lift out onto a plate.
Melt a little of the butter in the same pan and fry the eggs, spooning the butter over the yolks until the whites are set.
Meanwhile toast the white bread and spread with the rest of the butter.
Plate the eggs with the smoky mushrooms and buttered toast.

dishes.make_ahead: Bake the day before, ice on the day

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20 x 30cm tin. Beat 200g of the butter with the caster sugar until pale.
Beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla, then fold in the self-raising flour and 125ml of the milk.
Spread into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the remaining 150g butter with the icing sugar and the last 2 tbsp milk until fluffy and spread over the top.
Pipe WELCOME HOME JOEY across the cake with the blue writing icing.

dishes.make_ahead: Make up to a day ahead and keep in the fridge

steps.text: Whisk the cocoa and caster sugar with 100ml hot water until smooth.
Stir in the cold full cream milk and chill for an hour.
Stir again and pour into four tall glasses with a straw each.
Brew the ground coffee with the water in a filter coffee machine or pour-over.
Pour the coffee black into four mugs. No sugar.
